title: SWR: Contactor State Machine and Fault Response

standards_mappings.relationship_note: The rationale states the record was written from the clause's concept ('software safety requirements'). Where the same rationale also says that no clause text was reproduced or consulted, that is a RIGHTS statement about wording, not a statement about influence: the record took the concept's shape and not its words, which is why the clause is its derivation basis. It is not a conformance claim - no clause was audited against this record and no assessment was performed.

The rationale states the derivation explicitly ('software requirements and architecture'): this record was written from the clause's concept, or supplies the work product the clause expects, or consumes the one the clause produces. safety_class_disclaimer.not_a_project_published_artefact_reason: This requirement belongs to the fictional reference project this corpus declares in its synthetic_reference profile, not to the foxBMS 2 product. foxBMS 2 published no requirement of any kind with an identifier, and nothing was ever allocated to an ASIL on its behalf. It is the reference project's contactor state-machine requirement, written by this corpus. foxBMS 2 published no software safety requirement and allocated no ASIL.
safety_class_disclaimer.misreading_warning: A reader who sees an ASIL_D software safety requirement specifying OPEN -> PRECHARGE -> CLOSE -> HOLD with a 5 ms opening time mapped to ISO 26262 Part 6 Clause 7 with status `mapped` will conclude the state machine is a reviewed, allocated, verified safety behaviour. The four-state sequence is the reference project's construction and is not the sequence in the pinned source, which opens on fault and confirms feedback; the 5 ms is unmeasured; and no test here executes against it on target hardware.

derivation_basis.locator: src/app/driver/contactor/contactor.c:125-163 (CONT_CheckFeedback) for the feedback confirmation, src/app/engine/diag/diag.c:341-475 (DIAG_Handler) for the fault request that triggers the reaction, and src/app/engine/diag/cbs/diag_cbs_contactor.c:73-125 (DIAG_StringContactorFeedback) for the contactor diagnostic string. Pinned commit 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437. The four-state sequence and the 5 ms figure are the reference project's, not the source's.
derivation_basis.what_it_supports: That the pinned source confirms contactor feedback and opens on a fault request - the actuation behaviour this requirement obliges. It supports nothing about the state machine's states, the 5 ms figure, or the ASIL, and the chain it describes is longer than the 100 ms the goal allocates.

revision_history.description: Added safety_class_disclaimer, carrying no modification of the statement, the ASIL value, the allocation, the acceptance criteria or any standards mapping. The defect corrected is legibility: this record was already marked `profile: synthetic_reference` and, for the SYRs, already says in its own limitations field that it establishes nothing about the real project - but a reader skimming `artifact_type`, `asil` and `standards_mappings` sees a safety requirement at an ASIL with an ISO 26262 clause and status `mapped`, and reads it as an allocated, conformant safety obligation of the product. It is a requirement of the fictional reference project this corpus declares. derivation_basis names what the derivation actually rests on - for most of these, specific pinned file:line ranges, and for FB2-SAF-FSR-000004, FB2-HW-TSR-000004, FB2-SYS-SYR-000004 and FB2-SYS-SYR-000005, the explicit statement that there is no such source because the subject does not exist - and states what it does not support. No other field of the record was modified.

statement: The contactor driver shall execute state machine (OPEN -> PRECHARGE -> CLOSE -> HOLD) and open contactors within 5 ms of FAULT state request from SOA/DIAG.
rationale: Contactor software must respond to SOA violations within FTTI budget

acceptance_criteria.measure: Time from FAULT request to coil de-energize command

safety_allocation.mitigation: Feedback monitoring, independent SBC watchdog, state machine validation
